scope: PERF-03 local warm-open phase measurements and bounded validation scheduling
UI-07 audited loading stages and visible cancellation

performance.baseline: Same working tree with phase hooks, before cache scheduling refactor. Retains preceding Flight/replay fixes. This is not a comparison against clean HEAD.
performance.procedure: Five paired fresh-cache builds and five paired existing-cache opens; alternate before/after order. Elapsed monotonic clock and per-child wait4 RSS. Warm profiling enabled in both binaries; cold profiling disabled. Same cache identity, source corpus, machine, and correctness oracle.
performance.binary_scope: Measured before and after binaries are preserved by SHA-256. Final service progress/cancellation refinements do not execute in the direct-store perf_driver open path; cache scheduling and format are unchanged since measurement. Final workload/capture/browser checks exercise the final implementation.

raw_warm.scope: paired warm open, identical existing cache/corpus/machine; profiling enabled in both binaries

raw_cold.scope: five paired fresh-cache builds, same canonical 10M QTRB/512MiB Flight corpus; profiling disabled

performance.query_scope: 200 direct-analysis viewport and 200 indexed structured queries per binary; no UI frame-latency claim.
performance.profiling: QTRACE_UI_OPEN_PROFILE=1 emits nested/overlapping spans. The reader uses held descriptors and bounded pread, without an mmap phase. Every checksum, catalog truth validation, identity check, and corruption rebuild remains enforced.

loading.counter_semantics: Per-stage accounted input bytes, events and row work. Repeated passes count separately. Artifact total is independent. No unique-coverage percentage or ETA inferred.
loading.allocation_boundary: Progress notifications may allocate only outside a WorkGuard allocation scope; authorization records counters using atomics and defers notifications. Covered by focused regression.

analysis_cancellation.procedure: Observe the shared slot locked by a query, let the build run for 20 ms, close the workspace, join the query, require job.cancelled, empty slots, and released store Weak reference.
analysis_cancellation.scope: Single-run release diagnostics, not a cancellation latency gate. Deterministic blocked-slot regressions and existing concurrent cache-sharing/release tests also pass.

checks.command: QTRACE_CANCEL_REPORT=<retained Flight report> cargo test --release -p qtrace-service --lib close_cancels_active_analysis_on_large_capture -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1

regression_proof.blocked_register_and_call_tree_before_fi: Both tests returned successful results after workspace closure; both now return job.cancelled and release stores.

verification_notes: Full workspace tests pass; after the final progress-only allocation notification change, the affected service suite and clippy/fmt/generated checks pass again. The final browser harness reruns against the rebuilt service.
Initial concurrently compiled frontend run hit the existing 5 s test deadline. Unchanged focused test passed in 2.79 s; unchanged full frontend suite passed, with no deadline changes.
Retained capture timings are functional diagnostics and overlap other verification work; they are not before/after performance samples.
No new Android capture, tracer throughput, rich-workload performance gate, native file-dialog, high-zoom layout, or call-tree cumulative-memory claim. Existing reference baselines remain intact.
